definitions.explanation: The number four. This reading (よん) is more commonly used in modern Japanese than し because し sounds like {死|し} (death). よん is generally preferred when counting and in most compound numbers.

examples.japanese: {四|よん}{人|にん}で{食事|しょくじ}しました。
examples.english: We had a meal with four people.

examples.japanese: りんごが{四|よっ}つあります。
{四|よん}{十|じゅう}{五|ご}{分|ふん}です。
{一|いち}{週間|しゅうかん}は{七|なな}{日|にち}で、{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}は{四|よん}{週間|しゅうかん}です。
examples.english: One week has seven days, and one month has four weeks.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}の{家族|かぞく}は{四|よ}{人|にん}で、{父|ちち}と{母|はは}と{姉|あね}と{私|わたし}です。
examples.english: My family has four people: my father, mother, older sister, and me.

notes: Japanese has two readings for four: よん and し. よん is more common because し is homophonous with {死|し} (death), making it inauspicious. However, し is used in some set expressions like {四|し}{月|がつ} (shigatsu, April) and {四|し}{時|じ} (yoji, four o'clock—note this is an exception using よ). When counting with つ, it becomes {四|よっ}つ (yottsu).
